question: A METAR is:
option_a: A report of the weather conditions observed right now at an airport
option_b: A forecast of next week's weather
option_d: A list of airport radio frequencies

question: A TAF is different from a METAR because a TAF is:
option_a: A forecast of what the weather is expected to do
option_b: A report of what the weather is doing right now

question: In a US METAR, wind speed is given in:
option_a: Knots

question: In a US METAR, visibility is given in:
option_a: Statute miles

question: In a METAR, cloud heights are given in:
option_a: Feet above ground level

question: Yaw is the motion of a drone:
option_a: Rotating left or right about its vertical axis, so the nose points a new direction
option_b: Tilting nose up or nose down
option_c: Tilting left or right so it slides sideways

question: Pitch is the motion of a drone:
option_a: Tilting nose up or nose down, which moves it forward or backward
option_b: Rotating so the nose points a new direction
option_c: Tilting left or right so it slides sideways

question: Roll is the motion of a drone:
option_a: Tilting left or right so it slides sideways
option_b: Rotating so the nose points a new direction
option_c: Tilting nose up or nose down

question: On a Mode 2 controller, the LEFT stick controls:
option_a: Throttle (up and down) and yaw (turning the nose)

question: On a Mode 2 controller, the RIGHT stick controls:
option_a: Pitch (forward and back) and roll (left and right)

question: You push the RIGHT stick to the right. The drone will:
option_a: Roll right and slide to its right, with the nose still pointing the same direction
option_b: Spin to the right so the nose points right

question: You push the LEFT stick to the right. The drone will:
option_a: Yaw right, rotating so the nose points a new direction, without moving sideways
option_b: Slide to its right without turning

question: You are filming a runner and want to arc to the RIGHT around them while keeping them centered. You would push:
option_a: Right stick right, and left stick left at the same time

question: Throttle controls the drone's:
option_a: Altitude, up and down

question: If you take your thumbs off both sticks, the drone will:
option_a: Hold its position and hover, because the sticks spring back to center
option_d: Keep moving in the direction it was going

question: RTH stands for:
option_a: Return to Home

question: The four forces acting on a drone in flight are:
option_a: Lift, weight, thrust, and drag

question: The maximum altitude for most small drone operations is:
option_a: 400 feet above ground level

question: Under Part 107, the minimum flight visibility required is:
option_a: 3 statute miles

question: Under Part 107, the maximum groundspeed for a small drone is:
option_a: 100 miles per hour

question: VLOS stands for:
option_a: Visual line of sight, meaning you can see the aircraft with your own eyes

question: A drone must be registered with the FAA if it weighs more than:
option_a: 0.55 pounds, which is 250 grams
option_d: Drones never need to be registered

question: Part 107 is:
option_a: The FAA rules for flying a small drone for work or any non-recreational purpose

question: TRUST stands for:
option_a: The Recreational UAS Safety Test
option_c: Training for Regulated Unmanned Systems Transport

question: The main difference between TRUST and Part 107 is:
option_a: TRUST is for recreational flying, Part 107 is for work or other non-recreational flying
option_c: Part 107 is for children and TRUST is for adults
option_d: They are two names for the same test

question: You want to fly a drone to shoot video that the school will use to promote an event. This flight would fall under:
option_a: Part 107, because it is not purely recreational
option_b: TRUST, because you are a student
option_c: No rules, because it is at a school
option_d: Part 107 only if you are paid in cash

question: You are 15 years old and want to fly a drone just for fun at a park. What do you need?
option_a: TRUST, plus registration if the drone is over 0.55 pounds

question: The RPIC is the:
option_a: Remote Pilot in Command, the person responsible for the safety of the flight

question: In a METAR, temperature and dew point are given in:
option_a: Degrees Celsius

question: Under Part 107, the required distance from clouds is:
option_a: 500 feet below and 2,000 feet horizontally
